item.title: Corners bars and the World Series, how fans are taking in the game
item.description: Amanda Merkwae is watching the World Series at the bar with her parents ashes in her pocket. Her father passed this October and her mother died in January 2025. The two of them loved the Brewers, she said. "One of their favorite past times in retirement was just watching the game," said Merkwae, a Milwaukee resident, "and every time that I would call my mom on my daily drives, she would always start with how the Brewers played." Merkwae and her parents are watching the game form The Newport, a local bar in Milwaukee's Bay View neighborhood. The sold out American Family Field watch parties and crowds of people in the Deer District for Game 5 may grab attention. But all throughout Milwaukee there's a corner bar with a TV on and diehard fans watching the game. The Newport is a "beautiful towny Milwaukee bar," Merkwae said. There's wood paneling flanked by Christmas lights that are up year round – and free hot dogs. There's ruckus cheering that breaks out and a DJ who keeps commercial breaks interesting. Order Journal Sentinel Championship Book She said the vibes at the bar can't be found in any other city. Every night she is having conversations with other patrons about what games were like as a kid and what the championship run means to them. The Newport beats the big watch parties, she thinks. "I've had some pretty spectacular conversations where it just feels like we're in this together," she said, "also Miller Lite for like three dollars and free hot dogs." The Journal Sentinel was hopping around to different bars before Game 5 of the World Series. Merkwae said the next stop should be Club Garibaldi. Club Garibaldi is a literal corner bar at S. Superior Street and E. Russell Avenue. It's a classic bar that has the best of both worlds. It has that hometown feel with good brews on tap. At least that's how Lydia Chiappetti, a Milwaukee resident, described the bar. Those who don't drink can watch the game, eat some food, and play pinball, pool or darts. Her best game is pinball with darts and pool tied for her worst. She said the World Series run has felt like the time between Christmas and New Years. "No day counts, you're just eating out, staying up – I couldn't tell you what day of the week it is," Chiappetti said. She said she was born and raised on baseball. It helped her meet some of her best friends and is providing brand-new experiences as this is the Brewers first World Series appearance since 1982. Chiappetti has been splitting her time at a couple bars for the World Series, including Wolski's. She didn't think about going to any of the major watch parties. There's just too much crowd for her, and bartenders that know her face and can get her a beer quicker. item.title: DB Jay Timmons among Ohio State starters questionable for USC game
item.description: Along with quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson , Ohio State football could be without two more starters for the USC game on Oct. 31. Ohio State nickel back Jay Timmons and wide receiver Brandon Inniss are listed as questionable on the Buckeyes ' initial availability report, released by the Big Ten three days before the game. Sayin and Jackson are the only starters among seven Buckeyes already ruled out. Timmons made his first appearance in two games against Indiana on Oct. 17 , recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble. But Timmons was pulled from the lineup once again and missed Ohio State's final defensive drives due to an apparent injury. "He plans on traveling," Ohio State coach Ryan Day said Oct. 28. "We'll kind of see how the next couple of days go." After Inniss had missed the Maryland matchup on Oct. 10 with an undisclosed injury, he played the full game against Indiana , logging one catch for 6 yards. The senior is tied for third for the Buckeyes with 11 receptions this season for 158 yards and one touchdown. Freshman wide receiver Brock Boyd is also listed as questionable. Sayin and Jackson were expected to be out for the USC game, as Sayin is out "indefinitely" with an undisclosed injury he suffered in the fourth quarter of the Indiana game and Jackson underwent foot surgery, according to a report from ESPN on Oct. 21. Ohio State offensive lineman Austin Siereveld was notably left off the availability report after missing the previous two games due to illness. Day stated that Siereveld has returned to full practice this week, and he expects the senior to be an option, though is uncertain he'll be able to play the full game. The Buckeyes kick off at USC at 7:30 p.m. ET. bmackay@dispatch.com @brimackay15 This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: DB Jay Timmons among Ohio State starters questionable for USC game

item.title: Jacob Misiorowski battling mound at Tropicana Field in World Series Game 5
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL – It was Jacob Misiorowski versus the mound once again. The Milwaukee Brewers right-hander had troubles with his landing spot on the Tropicana Field mound right away in Game 5 of the World Series on Oct. 28, creating a fascinating subplot to follow given his issues with road mounds throughout the season. Eight pitches in, Misiorowski slipped as he threw a fastball to Junior Caminero and called time to reach down and toss a few chunks of clay off the mound where his left cleat dug in. The Rays grounds crew came out to fix the landing spot, then Misiorowski finished the rest of the inning, which included a slight slip on his final pitch. Misiorowski's footing was again loose while he warmed up for the top of the second, leading to four members of the grounds crew to rake, water and tamp the dirt. The same happened before the third. This is not the first time Misiorowski has dealt with this. On Aug. 2 in Anaheim, he dealt with a hard mound for much of the game and called it "probably one of the worst mounds I've had." Twenty-five days later in the rain at Citi Field , he slid all over. In his following outing at Wrigley Field, he was again frustrated with the landing spot. Pitching coach Chris Hook gave Misiorowski marching orders after that: No talking about mounds. It wasn't an issue the rest of the year, but Tropicana Field's mound encountered troubles one night before during Game 4 when Cam Booser needed it fixed. item.title: Pelicans Asking Price for Herb Jones Revealed
item.description: Herb Jones Pelicans Getty The New Orleans Pelicans‘ asking price in a potential trade sending away Herb Jones has been revealed, and it’s a high price. While it’s still early in the season, the Pelicans are 0-3, and it doesn’t feel like much is going to change, as they are one of the weakest teams in the Western Conference on paper and thus likely to miss the playoffs once again. That’s why the team’s front office is considering making moves, and one of them could be trading away Jones, one of the NBA’s top defensive forwards. Pelicans Want 2 First-Round Picks for Herb Jones According to Shamit Dua, the Pelicans want two first-round picks in a trade for Jones, but to this point, no other team has matched their asking price. “League sources say the Pelicans have held firm at an asking price near two first-round picks, though no team has met that figure. Many in the league believe Jones’ value will continue to go down if his minutes continue to be sporadic. Jones’ contract is also slated to jump next year from $14.9 million to $20.8 million. Nevertheless, several playoff teams view Jones as a valuable cultural and basketball fit,” Dua wrote. Jordan Poole Wants Out In addition to potentially trading Jones, Dua also reported that Pelicans guard Jordan Poole wants out and has informed the team that he is open to moving on. “Jones is not the only veteran whose future in New Orleans is uncertain. Sources say Jordan Poole has told the Pelicans he would be open to opportunities elsewhere. His preference raises a broader question about how many of the team’s veterans see their long-term future in New Orleans. Poole has also recorded more minutes than Jones in the last two contests,” Dua wrote. So, will the Pelicans make some moves? It feels like president of basketball operations Joe Dumars should be open to anything at this point, as the Pelicans seem like a lost cause and a team that should essentially be open to having a fire sale for any of its veteran players as they look to build around their young players. item.title: Lamar Jackson Returns To Practice, But Ravens Fans Should Stay Cautious
item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Lamar Jackson returned to practice as a full participant on Wednesday, giving the Baltimore Ravens a genuine spark of hope before their Sunday game against the Bills. However, coach Jesse Minter refuses to confirm a start date, stating that optimism rises only when the player can respond to physical demands. The team faces a tough test in Buffalo, and the clock is ticking on this ankle sprain. Jackson has missed three games since injuring his ankle in the win over the Tennessee Titans. His ability to plant his foot while running remains the critical hurdle. Minter noted on Monday that the quarterback will play only if he is healthy enough to perform at his required level. The situation is fluid, and the coaching staff is watching his recovery closely. The Practice Reality Wednesday marked a significant shift in the narrative surrounding Jackson’s injury. He joined the full practice session, which is a strong indicator that his rehab is progressing. Minter told reporters on Wednesday that the more Jackson can do and feel, the more optimistic the team becomes. Yet, the coach added a necessary caveat, saying, according to Fox Sports , “But again, we’ll kind of see how it goes throughout the week.” This cautious approach protects the team from false hope. The Ravens have faced similar cycles in the past where fans get excited only to see the star sit out. Jackson himself has been clear about the pain involved. He told reporters last week that he can play if he can feel the pain a little, but he cannot help the team if he is restricted or just standing there getting hit. History of Uncertainty Jackson has been less durable than peers like Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. The league often keeps injury details secret to prevent opponents from gaining an edge. This secrecy creates confusion for fans who want clear answers. Minter first stated Jackson was “dealing with a little bit of an ankle” injury on the day the quarterback got hurt, according to ESPN . Later, he explained that “some talks” occurred regarding Jackson’s return to that specific game. What This Means For Sunday The Ravens need their quarterback to lead a high-powered offense in Buffalo. Jackson’s unique running ability gives him a floor that few other quarterbacks can match. If he cannot move the way he needs to, the entire offensive strategy shifts. Minter emphasized that the decision rests on whether Jackson can play the way the team feels he needs to play. The team will not rush him back just to fill a roster spot. Expect the final decision to come late in the week. The Ravens play at Buffalo on Sunday, and the coaching staff will monitor Jackson’s progress daily. The injury is an ankle sprain, which is not a routine ailment for a mobile quarterback. Fans should stay ready for a potential change in game plan if Jackson cannot go.
